title: 〜だらけ
simpleExplanation: Noun + だらけ means "full of" or "covered with" something you do not want: 泥だらけ "covered in mud", 間違いだらけ "full of mistakes". It is always negative: you cannot say 花だらけ to praise a garden. It behaves like a noun or な-adjective: だらけだ, だらけの + noun, だらけで.
whenUsed: Everyday complaints and vivid descriptions: rooms, clothes, essays, roads. In writing it appears in descriptive passages. Common nouns: 泥, ごみ, 傷, 間違い, ほこり, 血, しわ, 借金.
formation: Noun + だらけ + だ / です
Noun + だらけ + の + Noun (泥だらけの靴)
Noun + だらけになる (become covered in)

rows.label: 〜だらけ
cells: Many unwanted things or marks, anywhere

rows.label: 〜まみれ (N2)
cells: A liquid or powder sticking to a surface

examples.ja: 子供たちは泥だらけになって帰ってきた。
examples.reading: こどもたちはどろだらけになってかえってきた。
examples.en: The kids came home covered in mud.
examples.note: だらけになる: became covered in mud.

examples.ja: この作文は間違いだらけだ。
examples.reading: このさくぶんはまちがいだらけだ。
examples.en: This essay is full of mistakes.

examples.ja: 部屋はほこりだらけで、掃除が大変だった。
examples.reading: へやはほこりだらけで、そうじがたいへんだった。
examples.en: The room was full of dust and cleaning was hard.
examples.note: だらけで connective: dust everywhere, so cleaning was hard.

examples.ja: 事故の後、車は傷だらけになっていた。
examples.reading: じこのあと、くるまはきずだらけになっていた。
examples.en: After the accident, the car was covered in scratches.
examples.note: 傷だらけ = covered in scratches or wounds.

examples.ja: 彼は借金だらけで、生活が苦しいらしい。
examples.reading: かれはしゃっきんだらけで、せいかつがくるしいらしい。
examples.en: He is deep in debt and apparently struggling to make ends meet.

similarGrammar.difference: Only for liquids or particles clinging to a surface (血まみれ, 泥まみれ). だらけ is broader and also abstract.
Neutral 'full of', usable for good things (人でいっぱい, 喜びでいっぱい).
'-ish' (油っぽい = greasy). Describes a quality, not being covered.

commonMistakes.wrong: 庭は花だらけできれいだ。
commonMistakes.right: 庭は花でいっぱいできれいだ。
commonMistakes.why: だらけ is negative and cannot describe something pleasant.
Before a noun, だらけ takes の, not な.

commonMistakes.wrong: この文章は間違いだらけがある。
commonMistakes.right: この文章は間違いだらけだ。
commonMistakes.why: だらけ already means 'full of'; it does not combine with がある.

usageNotes: だらけ can be used jokingly or affectionately about oneself: 失敗だらけの人生.
It attaches only to nouns; verbs and adjectives need a noun form first.
In 読解, 傷だらけ and 間違いだらけ appear in descriptions of condition.
jlptTips: If the noun is something unpleasant (泥, ごみ, 傷, 間違い) and the sense is 'all over', だらけ is right.
Choices may include まみれ; if the noun is not a liquid/powder (e.g. 間違い), only だらけ works.
Watch the connector to a following noun: だらけの, never だらけな.
